assumptions: The business begins without exclusive broker, importer, supplier, registry-integration, or verifier contracts because none are evidenced in the bound research.
The founder keeps full-time employment and is limited to the canonical maximum of five hours per day until objective traction and runway conditions are met.
Unknown willingness to pay, support load, CAC, renewal, and data-reuse rights remain unresolved uncertainty rather than proof of failure.
The product does not act as an accredited verifier and cannot transfer the authorised declarant's statutory responsibility.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Signed broker and verifier commitments; paid importer pilots at the proposed price; measured supplier completion, remediation hours, CAC, payback, renewal, gross margin, and actual-versus-default savings; contractual cross-importer data rights; and evidence that the workflow produces materially fewer errors or faster verifier acceptance than the Commission registry and incumbent products.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: The mandatory CBAM evidence and certificate workflow creates a real coordination problem, but the proposed insight is not proprietary: the Commission registry already supports upload-once sharing and report population, while the statutory roles remain with the operator, verifier, and declarant. The candidate identifies workflow friction but overstates the distinctiveness of becoming its evidence custodian.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Above-threshold importers face a compulsory declaration, certificate spend, correction risk, and recurring records burden, so the underlying pain is material and budget-linked. However, the evidence establishes the obligation rather than willingness to buy this product at the proposed recurring price, and existing registry, ERP, consultant, broker, and specialist routes may already satisfy much of the job.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Annual software and managed-service revenue could recur, and the stated capital requirement is compatible with a bootstrap test. The attractive margin, payback, CAC, renewal, supplier-pack revenue, and certificate-savings assumptions are all unvalidated; multilingual supplier remediation, methodology changes, verifier questions, security review, and liability insurance could make the offer service-heavy. Reaching 150 importers would also require roughly 9.4% of the measured Polish above-threshold population before segment and competitive exclusions.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Central European industrial importers form a legible beachhead with a clear regulatory trigger, but the adopted 50-tonne threshold removed about 90% of importers and the research found only 1,589 Polish importers above it in 2024. The reachable mid-market subset lacking incumbent tooling is unknown, so Poland is focused but may be too narrow for the proposed penetration path without early regional expansion.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: The candidate enters an occupied category against the official registry, SAP, PwC, CBAMBOO, and likely broker or consultancy bundles. It has no exclusive data, registry, broker, supplier, or verifier position and cannot assume the declarant's statutory liability, leaving no demonstrated route to dominate even the Polish wedge.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A functioning importer-supplier workflow could extend across Central Europe and additional covered supply chains, and reusable integrations may lower subsequent expansion cost. Yet reuse rights, supplier overlap, geographic market size, and adjacency beyond the same CBAM workflow are unproven, while the official registry and incumbent suites can expand over the same paths.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Four-year retention and embedded integrations can create some switching friction, but the central evidence is permission-gated, non-exclusive, and tied to a government registry. No consent for cross-importer reuse, exclusive channel, proprietary outcome labels, or validated accuracy advantage is established, so the proposed data graph is not yet an ownable moat and incumbent bundling can compress margins.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: A focused Central European interface and hands-on exception handling could be more convenient than broad enterprise tooling for some importers. The research does not establish a material advantage in price, accuracy, speed, verifier acceptance, savings, or distribution, and the official registry plus existing vendors already cover the main collection, validation, audit, and reporting functions.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: The definitive regime, published certificate prices, ongoing rule updates, January 2027 verification timing, and September 2027 first filing deadline create a strong implementation window and measurable urgency. That same timing has already attracted mature vendors, while high actual-emissions reporting in 2025 indicates many target importers formed supplier-data processes before this entrant.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Customs brokers and trade accountants are a plausible concentrated route that avoids founder-led mass selling, but there is no signed reseller, measured lead flow, commission model, exclusivity, or evidence that channels will prefer this product over their own service bundles and incumbent tools. Enterprise trust, security, and liability review may also make customer acquisition slow for a part-time new entrant.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The software and data-normalization core fits the founder's technical skills and starting capital, and accredited work can be contracted rather than performed by the founder. Delivery nonetheless depends on cooperative foreign suppliers and accredited verifiers, while exceptions, methodology maintenance, confidentiality, professional liability, and partner enablement may exceed a five-hour daily ceiling. The startup cannot repair missing source data or independently produce the legally sufficient verified result.

highest_value_structural_change: Secure a verifier-backed, contractually exclusive broker channel for a narrow importer segment and make the product the accepted exception-resolution and evidence-control standard, with explicit supplier reuse rights and validated outcome improvement; this would replace generic custody with a controlled distribution and trust mechanism.
main_structural_strength: A mandatory, recurring regulatory process links importer pain to a measurable certificate liability, while the technical evidence-normalization product can be tested with modest capital and fits the founder's data-science strengths.
primary_score_limiter: The candidate does not currently own or control the critical mechanism: suppliers create the data, accredited verifiers validate it, declarants retain liability, and the Commission registry already performs cross-declarant sharing, leaving the startup as a replaceable workflow layer without exclusive rights or a proven channel.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: The Commission's O3CI registry already provides the thesis's upload-once, share-with-many function and can auto-populate reports; SAP, PwC, and CBAMBOO also offer overlapping workflows, while 95% of above-threshold importers were already reporting actual emissions by Q3 2025.
